First, note that the series can be written as

$$
4\cdot {\sum }_{n=8}^{\infty }\frac{1}{n(n+1)}.
$$

Using partial fractions we can write the series as

$$
4\cdot {\sum }_{n=8}^{\infty }(\frac{1}{n}-\frac{1}{n+1}).
$$

Computing the first few partial sums, starting with $n=8,$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{s}_{8} & =4\cdot [(\frac{1}{8}-\frac{1}{9})] \\ {s}_{9} & =4\cdot [(\frac{1}{8}-\cancel{\frac{1}{9}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{9}}-\frac{1}{10})] \\ {s}_{10} & =4\cdot [(\frac{1}{8}-\cancel{\frac{1}{9}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{9}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{10}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{10}}-\frac{1}{11})] \\ {s}_{11} & =4\cdot [(\frac{1}{8}-\cancel{\frac{1}{9}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{9}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{10}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{10}}-\cancel{\frac{1}{11}})+(\cancel{\frac{1}{11}}-\frac{1}{12})].\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that for each partial sum, we always end up canceling all terms with the exception of the first and last terms. Therefore, the $N$th partial sum is

$$
{s}_{N}=4\cdot [\frac{1}{8}-\frac{1}{N+1}].
$$

Finally, we can determine the sum of the series by taking the limit of ${s}_{N}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=8}^{\infty }\frac{4}{n(n+1)} & ={lim}_{N\to \infty }{s}_{N} \\  & ={lim}_{N\to \infty }4\cdot [\frac{1}{8}-\frac{1}{N+1}] \\  & =4\cdot [\frac{1}{8}-0] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
